narration.authorization: User explicitly approved natural synthetic narration in English and French on 2026-10-22.
narration.disclosure: Stock synthetic voices. Not a recording of a human actor and not a clone of any historical speaker. Historical quotations remain genuine archive recordings.
narration.processing: Kokoro natural-speed synthesis, native silence trim, 8 ms/45 ms click fades, 40 ms lead and 80 ms tail, resample to 48 kHz stereo PCM16. No post-synthesis time compression or word truncation. Normalize and duck beneath the film in the final mix.

spaceXContext: The CRS-6 still photograph is removed. This edition uses actual moving Falcon Heavy STP-2 launch and side-booster landing footage from 2019, followed by actual Falcon 9 Sentinel-6 landing footage from 2020. Different missions, not Starship catches or the first successful Falcon 9 return.
historicalContext: Dinosaurs did not immediately follow Earth’s formation and were not the first life. The narrative jumps across deep time; humans appear millions of years after non-avian dinosaurs.
The tool-making scene is a fictional 1912 film reconstruction; fire-making is a modern NPS demonstration. No camera footage from prehistory is claimed.
Wernher von Braun was a Nazi Party and SS member. V2 production used forced labor. His NASA team later developed Saturn V.
The V1 is a cruise missile. The V2 film shows captured German hardware tested at White Sands in 1946.
The Sputnik flight spare was filmed in 2017, with the genuine archived satellite signal. Gagarin’s Russian voice is genuine.
Saturn V was approximately 111 metres tall and the tallest rocket yet flown during the Apollo era; no present-day largest-rocket claim is made.
Challenger and Columbia were separate Shuttle losses, in 1986 and 2003. Neither was the final Shuttle mission.
Curiosity is active hardware in this story, not described as abandoned or shut down. The equipment catalogue remains empty until Hugo provides validated histories.
The final rover-to-orbit-to-solar-system sequence is an editorial join of existing NASA videos, not one physically continuous camera journey.
offlineContext: The user may download the complete shared 720p video, both mixed audio languages and both progressive fallbacks. Files are local, size/hash verified and marked ready only after completion; browser storage persistence is best effort.
